posts.name: bluedarky
posts.cooked:
I have to admit, despite all the arguments against it, I find the superhuman charisma for Greatest Legacy to be somewhat legit.

America's Greatest Legacy allows him to inspire a hero to shrug off some damage and use a power immediately, now whilst this makes sense for some heroes (Bunker, Unity, Tachyon, ect.) for others it makes no thematic sense that someone could inspire them to keep going like that (Chrono-Ranger, Absolute Zero, The Scholar, Fanatic, ect.)  and I know, I know, there's going to be some level of gameplay and story segregation in a game like this but still...

posts.name: Estelindis
posts.cooked:
The bio for Greatest Legacy says that his new power was super-sharp sight, making him very good with a gun.  The charisma does make sense, though I prefer to think of it as something that Legacy achieves himself through the way he chooses to act, not a hereditary power.

I find the concept of the Legacy powers fascinating.  What ensures that only the firstborn gets the power?  It has to be something other than genetics, because genes don't "know" which child is the firstborn.

posts.name: Estelindis
posts.cooked: It's strongly implied that Pauline Felicia's death in the Iron Legacy timeline ends the Legacy line forever, in a way that means no powers will ever be passed down again.  It's not just losing his daughter that makes Paul VIII despair but the fact that he's the last one who will ever have his family powers.  I'm not saying that, if her death didn't end the line conclusively, he'd be callous enough to go "oh, no worries, guess I'll just have another child!"  However, it would be a single loss rather than the double loss he seems to experience.  That said, I agree that there's a lot that we don't know.  Has every Legacy only had one child, either by choice or because, for some weird genetic-magic reason, they could only have one child?  If not, did they have some normal children after the superpowered ones?  All this and more is in the realm of the unknown.
